inputs.share_count_basis: 1,171.49m shares in issue excluding 12.13m treasury shares (H1 FY2026 interim report, as at 25 Aug 2026) plus 14.87m dilutive options and restricted shares (H1 FY2026 diluted-EPS note) = 1,186.4m fully diluted. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment expense' RMB51,617k (line 4219). HK net-share-settlement equity-award taxes are nil (EquityAwardTaxes kpi 0 every year).
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10T03:38Z). Cross-check via USD legs: HKD=X 7.8472 / CNY=X 6.683 = 1.1742, a 0.2% tie, confirming direction (1 CNY buys ~1.17 HKD). No CNY-denominated dual listing to parity-check against. Statements are RMB ('RMB'000' throughout); the HKEX quote is HKD. Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX Friday session; Yahoo chart API, fetched 2026-10-11)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5%, one rate for all three scenarios (risk charged in the flows via scenario weights, not stacked in the rate). Flows are RMB-reported but ~63% of revenue is earned outside China, so the risk-free rate is revenue-blended: CGB 10y ~1.8% (China ~37%), Bund ~2.7% (EMEA ~37%), UST ~4.2% (Americas ~25%) -> ~2.6%. ERP 6.0%, levered beta 1.25 for a cyclical Tier-1 auto supplier -> cost of equity ~10.1%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.1% (FY2025 interest paid RMB323m on ~RMB9bn mostly floating multi-currency borrowings), ~2.6% after tax. Target D/V ~20% (gross debt RMB9.0bn vs market cap ~RMB23.4bn) -> ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB96.8m (20.3 current + 76.6 non-current, 30 Jun 2026) included in total_debt; lease principal (RMB21.8m FY2025) NOT deducted from flows; right-of-use depreciation (RMB44.8m) left inside D&A. Immaterial either way (<0.1% of EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book value RMB1,070.4m (30 Jun 2026). NCI takes ~2-3% of group profit (FY2025 RMB78.0m of RMB2,770.1m; H1 FY2026 RMB30.8m of RMB1,464.9m), so book is a fair proxy (~13x NCI earnings).
inputs.interest_income_treatment: interest_income set to 0 in the owner-FCF formula because reported FCF ALREADY excludes it: Minth's cash flow statement adjusts investment income (RMB206.3m FY2025) out of operating cash flow and books interest received in investing. Deducting it again would double-strip. The matching assets (cash, time deposits, structured deposits) are in the bridge, so the matching-asset rule holds.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Adjusted EBITDA = PBT + interest expense - investment income - share of JV/associate results - other gains and losses + D&A (PPE dep + ROU dep + intangibles amortisation) + SBC. FY2025: 3,295.9 + 324.9 - 206.3 - 28.4 - 278.7 + 1,699.3 + 51.6 = RMB4,858m, 18.9% of revenue. FY2024: 19.9%. H1 FY2026 (SBC estimated ~25): ~2,651m, 19.8%; H1 FY2025 ~19.5%. Other income (largely government grants, RMB303m FY2025) is kept inside EBITDA as recurring for a China-domiciled manufacturer; other gains and losses (FV changes on investments and derivatives, FX) are excluded as non-operating.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, scenario-weighted, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (currency, leases, NCI, matching assets, SBC-near-zero). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: Minth is an operating auto-parts manufacturer (body structure / battery housings, metal & trim, aluminium, plastics) whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; no prior valuation or MEMORY.md entry exists. OWNER FCF FY2025: OCF 4,912.3 - capex 2,313.0 (PPE 2,209.8 + intangibles 103.3) = reported FCF 2,599.2; less SBC 51.6 = 2,547.6. That base is flattered by a +RMB489m working-capital release in FY2025 (vs -RMB812m in FY2024) and by RMB265.5m of government asset subsidies that are booked in investing, not netted against capex; the component build does not carry either forward. FCF is unlevered (interest paid sits in financing). CAPEX: H1 FY2026 capex RMB1,642m = 12.2% of revenue vs 8.0% in H1 FY2025 -- management's 'staged increase' for North America (Mexico, Canada, Alabama), Europe, Southeast Asia and Morocco is visible, so the base path starts at 11% and glides to 8%. BUYBACKS: small (RMB15.6m FY2025, RMB25.8m H1 FY2026, 12.13m treasury shares held) and RMB405.7m of option exercise proceeds were RECEIVED in FY2025 -- the flat share count is a modelling convention, not something the company is funding. EQUITY BRIDGE: see equity_bridge (all at 30 Jun 2026). Net debt 766.0 = borrowings 8,951.0 + leases 96.8 - cash 4,524.6 - non-pledged time deposits 2,773.3 (current 1,074.4 less pledged 203.6, plus non-current 1,902.5) - structured deposits 983.9 (FVTPL note 15). Pledged deposits (RMB203.6m, backing bills) and FVOCI bills receivable are left in working capital. GUIDANCE: no company revenue/earnings guidance; management guides global light-vehicle sales -2 to -3% in 2026 and a staged capex increase. H1 FY2026 revenue +9.1%, attributable profit +12.3%.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.5% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 15.6% and EPS 3yr CAGR 21.2%: book growth lags because ~25-40% of earnings were paid out and FY2021-22 were heavy-capex, low-return years (ROE ~9%). Revenue growth is the better guide to the near-term top line; equity CAGR is used as the conservative anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC) was negative in FY2020 (-265.9), FY2021 (-1,927.8) and FY2022 (-1,550.7) during the capacity build-out, then 75.3 (FY2023), 1,293.4 (FY2024) and 2,547.6 (FY2025). SBC is ~0.2% of revenue, so reported and owner FCF CAGRs would be essentially identical -- SBC is not a growth-funding issue here; capex intensity is.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 8% = H1 +9.1% tempered for a weaker H2 auto backdrop (management: global LV sales -2-3%); battery-housing and EMEA content gains keep growth above the industry into FY2027, decaying to 3% by year 9.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA 19.3-19.5%: between FY2025 18.9% and H1 FY2026 ~19.8%; localisation ramp costs and OEM price-downs offset operating leverage, so no expansion is assumed.
base.capex_rationale: H1 FY2026 capex ran 12.2% of revenue on the North America/Europe/Morocco build; 11% for FY2026 falling to a sustaining 8% (vs D&A 7.2%) by year 7.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash tax ~16% of EBIT (HNTE 15% in China); rising to 19% as the profit mix shifts to Europe and the Americas.

scenario_narratives.base: Minth keeps compounding content per vehicle faster than global production: battery housings and body-structure parts for VW, BMW, Toyota, BYD, Chery and Changan carry FY2026 revenue up ~8% against a flat-to-down industry, with EMEA the engine and China domestic flat. Margins hold near 19.5% EBITDA as operating leverage is spent on localisation ramp costs in Mexico, Canada, Alabama, Serbia and Morocco and on OEM annual price-downs. Capex stays elevated (11% of revenue) through FY2027 for the overseas build, then falls to a sustaining 8%. The 'second growth curve' (robotics, eVTOL, AI liquid cooling) is given no explicit value.
scenario_narratives.bull: The GLOCAL footprint turns tariff fragmentation into share gains: European BEV adoption and Chinese brands' overseas localisation drive battery-housing volumes, North American energy-storage and Toyota programmes ramp, and new-business revenue (AI-server liquid cooling, robotics structures) becomes material by FY2029. Revenue grows ~10% a year for five years and EBITDA margin climbs to 21% on European battery-housing scale and capex returning to 8% once the build-out is absorbed.
scenario_narratives.bear: The auto cycle and policy turn together: China's domestic price war deepens and squeezes supplier pricing, European EV subsidies lapse, US tariffs on Mexican content raise costs at the new plants, and a major battery-housing platform (VW or a Chinese NEV maker) is in-sourced or re-sourced. Revenue stalls in FY2027 and grows only with inflation thereafter; EBITDA margin compresses to ~17% (the FY2021-22 trough territory) while the overseas plants already committed run underutilised, pushing D&A to 7.4% of revenue.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): a highly cyclical Tier-1 supplier with material customer/platform concentration in its fastest-growing segment, live US tariff and EU subsidy policy risk, and management itself guiding the 2026 industry down 2-3%. Base 50%: H1 FY2026 (+9.1% revenue, +12.3% profit) is tracking the base path. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull case needs EMEA EV demand, North American localisation and the unproven second-growth-curve businesses all to deliver at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Minth as a cyclical global auto-parts manufacturer on unlevered owner FCF built from components, with capex intensity -- not SBC -- the dominant judgment. Risk is charged once, through 25/50/25 scenario weights at a single 8.5% revenue-blended WACC, and the terminal value is capped at 10-13x FCF to reflect cyclicality. Treasury assets (time and structured deposits, equity investments, JVs) sit in the bridge because their income is excluded from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex intensity: the H1 FY2026 jump to 12.2% of revenue; if the overseas build runs at 11-12% for longer than two years, owner FCF stays near half of FY2025's level
EBITDA margin: each 1pp of margin is ~RMB260m of EBITDA in FY2026; the FY2021-22 trough was well below today's 19%
Customer/platform concentration in battery housings (third-party estimates: top-5 customers ~45-50% of revenue)
Tariff and EV-subsidy policy (US content rules on Mexican production, EU subsidy continuity)
CNY/HKD rate: per-share HKD values move one-for-one with it; refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate
Working-capital reversal: FY2025 owner FCF was flattered by a +RMB489m working-capital release
